hypothesis: Handcrafted forensic feature representations (noise, edge, texture, compression, and frequency-domain descriptors) combined with shallow classifiers (logistic regression, SVMs, and tree ensembles) trained on the Chapter 4 dataset can (1) achieve substantially better-than-random detection of watermark removal and (2) reveal systematic failure modes that usefully inform the design of later deep models.

baseline.name: Pixel-only logistic regression baseline
baseline.description: A regularized logistic regression classifier trained on aggressively downsampled raw pixel intensities (no handcrafted or frequency-domain features) to detect watermark removal, using the Chapter 4 image dataset and a fixed train/validation/test split.

treatment.name: Classical forensic feature baselines
treatment.description: A family of shallow models (logistic regression, linear SVM, RBF SVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Trees) trained on handcrafted spatial, compression, and frequency-domain feature vectors to detect watermark removal on the same dataset and splits as the pixel-only baseline.

features: Noise statistics: global and block-wise noise estimates via wavelet-based noise level or high-pass residuals
Edge statistics: Canny edge density, gradient histograms (e.g., 8-bin orientation histogram), edge connectivity metrics
Texture descriptors: Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) features (contrast, homogeneity, energy, correlation) computed on 4 directions; Local Binary Patterns (LBP) histograms
Compression artifacts: JPEG quantization artifact metrics (e.g., DCT coefficient histograms per block, blocking artifact measures), estimated JPEG quality factor where applicable
Frequency-domain features: 2D DCT low/mid/high-frequency band energies; radial power spectrum statistics from FFT magnitude; simple wavelet subband energies

shared_configuration.feature_normalization: StandardScaler (zero mean, unit variance) fitted on training set only; applied to train/val/test.
shared_configuration.dimensionality_reduction_optional: PCA to retain 95% variance as an optional ablation; if used, PCA is fit on training set only.
shared_configuration.data_split: Identical stratified split as baseline using precomputed indices from Chapter 4 dataset pipeline.

workloads.description: Supervised binary classification of watermark removal on still images from the Chapter 4 dataset, using a standardized set of watermarking schemes and removal attacks.
workloads.input_source: Repository dataset generated in Chapter 4, e.g., `data/ch4_dataset/images/` with manifest `data/ch4_dataset/metadata.csv`.

input_constraints.resolution: Original resolutions; feature pipeline will internally resize where required (e.g., to 256x256) using deterministic interpolation.

attack_families: Classical image processing (blurs, noise, affine transforms)
Compression/transcoding (JPEG re-save at varying quality, resizing + re-encoding)
Generative/inpainting-based edits (where available from Chapter 4 pipeline)

workloads.description: Evaluate the same trained models on predefined held-out distributions and attack families to study baseline robustness and failure modes.
workloads.input_source: Alternative splits or subsets defined in Chapter 4, e.g., `data/ch4_dataset/splits/cross_domain_test.csv`.
workloads.task_definition: Apply models trained on main training split to these held-out distributions without further fine-tuning; report all evaluation metrics per distribution and attack family.

data_controls.fixed_splits: Use precomputed `train_ids.csv`, `val_ids.csv`, `test_ids.csv` shipped with the Chapter 4 dataset to ensure all baselines share identical samples.
data_controls.stratification: Verify equivalent class proportions across train/val/test (within ±1% absolute) using a pre-check script.
data_controls.label_consistency: Assert that all examples have a single unambiguous label after mapping status to positive/negative; drop or log any conflicting rows.

preprocessing_controls.image_loading: Use OpenCV or Pillow with explicit color ordering (BGR→RGB or direct grayscale) documented and fixed.
preprocessing_controls.resize_policy: If resizing, use bilinear interpolation for downsampling and bicubic for upsampling; keep consistent across runs.
preprocessing_controls.color_space: For most features, use luminance or grayscale; when RGB is used (e.g., for texture), document the channel handling.

training_controls.cross_validation_for_hyperparams: Use nested or fixed 5-fold cross-validation on training set only; validation/test sets are never used for hyperparameter search.
training_controls.class_weights: Use `class_weight='balanced'` where supported; otherwise, handle imbalance by resampling within training folds only.
training_controls.early_stopping: Not applicable to scikit-learn shallow models except where implemented; if used (e.g., gradient boosting), configure deterministic criteria.

compute_controls.hardware: CPU-only reference runs; if GPU is available, only used for feature extraction acceleration when numerically equivalent.
compute_controls.parallelism: Cap scikit-learn `n_jobs` to a documented value (e.g., 8) for reproducible timing and resource usage.

metrics.name: brier_score
metrics.unit: mean squared error of probabilistic predictions

metrics.name: feature_importance_gini
metrics.unit: unitless importance scores normalized to sum to 1 (for tree ensembles)

metrics.name: coefficients_magnitude_logreg
metrics.unit: absolute coefficient values per feature (unitless, feature-scale dependent)

primary.description: For at least one forensic-feature treatment model, achieve statistically significant improvement over the pixel-only logistic regression baseline on ROC-AUC and F1 for the positive (watermark-removed) class on the main test set.
primary.statistical_test: Two-sided DeLong test for ROC-AUC difference; bootstrap confidence intervals for F1 difference.

secondary.description: Identify at least three distinct, interpretable feature groups (e.g., noise, edges, texture, compression, frequency) that show non-trivial importance or coefficient magnitude and that correlate with specific attack types or content categories.
secondary.operationalization: Analyze learned coefficients (logistic regression) and feature importances (Random Forest/Gradient Boosting), cluster by feature group, and document patterns in the experiment report.

secondary.description: Demonstrate reproducibility of metrics across reruns within narrow bounds.
secondary.operationalization: Repeat full training + evaluation pipeline 3 times with same seeds and environment; require variation in ROC-AUC and F1 to be ≤ 0.01 absolute across runs.

guardrails.description: Ensure false positive rate on clearly negative samples (intact or never-watermarked images without any watermark-related processing) stays below a risk-aware threshold to avoid unrealistic baselines.

failure_modes.name: Overfitting to specific watermarking/removal pipeline artifacts
failure_modes.description: Models may learn idiosyncratic signatures of the synthetic watermark embedding or removal implementation from Chapter 4 rather than generalizable cues, leading to degraded performance on the cross-distribution workload or new attack families.
failure_modes.detection: Significant drop in ROC-AUC or F1 (>0.15 absolute) when comparing main test set vs. cross-distribution test subsets.

failure_modes.name: Content-type bias
failure_modes.description: Models might key on content category (e.g., photos vs. graphics) if watermarking/removal distributions differ across categories.
failure_modes.detection: Per-category stratified metrics reveal large performance disparities; e.g., recall difference >0.2 between content types.

failure_modes.name: Label leakage via preprocessing or metadata
failure_modes.description: If file naming, resolution, or compression level correlates strongly with label, models might exploit these rather than true forensic cues.
failure_modes.detection: Simple baselines using only trivial metadata (resolution, file size, JPEG quality estimate) achieving similar performance to full forensic models.

failure_modes.name: Non-reproducible results due to nondeterminism
failure_modes.description: Differences in BLAS backends, library versions, or parallelism settings may cause small numeric differences that accumulate in model selection.
failure_modes.detection: More than ±0.02 absolute variation in ROC-AUC or F1 across three independent runs in an ostensibly identical environment.

failure_modes.name: Spurious feature correlations masking true signal
failure_modes.description: Highly correlated feature groups (e.g., overlapping texture and noise metrics) can make interpretation of individual feature importance misleading.
failure_modes.detection: High pairwise feature correlations (|r|>0.9) combined with unstable importance rankings across bootstrap resamples.
